Compute pathway activity scores

compute.pathway.activity.Rd

This function computes pathway activity scores from log-normalized gene expression data with decoupleR (Badia-i-Mompel et al., 2022), based on the PROGENy resource (Schubert et al., 2018). By default the univariate linear model ("ulm") is used. Optionally, it also performs Gene Set Variation Analysis (GSVA) using hallmark signatures or any user-provided gene sets.

Usage

compute.pathway.activity(
  counts_norm,
  gene_sets = NULL,
  paths = NULL,
  method = "ulm",
  scale = TRUE,
  batch = NULL,
  return = TRUE,
  file_name = NULL
)

Arguments

counts_norm

A numeric matrix of log-normalized gene expression values (e.g. log2(TPM + 1)) with genes (symbols) as rows and samples as columns. A warning is given if it has values above 20, which log2(TPM + 1) cannot reach.

gene_sets

A named list of gene sets (character vectors of gene symbols; e.g., hallmark signatures or user-defined sets). If provided, GSVA scores will be computed for these sets. Default is NULL.

paths

A data frame describing the pathway-gene interactions (columns source, target, weight) for use with PROGENy. If NULL, the human PROGENy resource (top 500 genes) is used and cached in Results/Pathways_collection_PROGENy.csv (also when return = FALSE, so that it is downloaded only once). A message gives the number of pathways and interactions of the cached file and the date it was saved; a cached file that is empty or lacks the needed columns is not used (the collection is downloaded again, with a warning). Delete the file to download the collection again.

method

Character. The decoupleR statistic used to score the PROGENy pathways: "ulm" (univariate linear model, default), "mlm" (multivariate linear model), "wsum" (weighted sum) or "consensus" (consensus of the three). The gene sets of gene_sets are always scored with GSVA.

scale

Logical. If TRUE (default), each pathway is z-scored across the samples. The scaled scores of a sample then depend on the other samples given in the same call; use scale = FALSE to get scores that can be compared between separate calls (e.g. a training and a test set). With fewer than three samples the scores are not scaled (a message is given).

batch

Optional vector with the cohort of each sample, in the column order of counts_norm (if it is named, it is matched to the samples by name instead). It is always treated as categorical. If given, the samples are split by cohort, the pathway activities (PROGENy and, if requested, GSVA) are computed and scaled (see scale) separately in each cohort, and the results are joined in the sample order of counts_norm; the output has the same form as without batch. Pathways or gene sets that cannot be scored in every cohort are left out (with a message). Default is NULL (single cohort); a vector with only one cohort is treated the same way.

return

Logical; if TRUE, saves the score matrices in Results/ folder. Default is TRUE.

file_name

Optional character suffix used when writing output CSV files (Results/Pathway_matrix_PROGENy_<file_name>.csv and Results/Pathway_matrix_GSVA_<file_name>.csv; without it, Results/Pathway_matrix_PROGENy.csv and Results/Pathway_matrix_GSVA.csv).

Value

If gene_sets is NULL, a data frame of PROGENy pathway activity scores (samples as rows, pathways as columns), scaled if scale = TRUE. If gene_sets is provided, a list with two elements:

  • PROGENy: A data frame of PROGENy pathway activity scores.

  • GSVA: A data frame of GSVA scores based on the provided gene sets.

Column names are made syntactically valid with make.names() (e.g. JAK.STAT), in the returned tables and in the saved files. Pathways with fewer than 5 of their genes in the data, and gene sets that GSVA cannot score, are left out with a message.

References

Schubert M, Klinger B, Kluenemann M, Sieber A, Uhlitz F, Sauer S, Garnett MJ, Bluethgen N, Saez-Rodriguez J. Perturbation-response genes reveal signaling footprints in cancer gene expression. Nature Communications. 2018. doi:10.1038/s41467-017-02391-6

Badia-i-Mompel, P. et al. (2022). decoupleR: ensemble of computational methods to infer biological activities from omics data. Bioinformatics Advances, 2(1), vbac016. https://doi.org/10.1093/bioadv/vbac016

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Compute only PROGENy activities (downloads the PROGENy model from OmniPath)
data("counts.norm.tuto")
pathways <- compute.pathway.activity(counts.norm.tuto)
} # }
